questionText:

List-I (UN Body)
(A) Security Council
(B) General Assembly
(C) Secretariat
(D) Economic and Social Council

List-II (Composition)
(I) International staff servicing the other principal organs, headed by the Secretary-General, who is appointed by the General Assembly on the recommendation of the Security Council.
(II) Member states elected by the General Assembly for overlapping three-year terms - 54 seats based on geographical representation.
(III) Fifteen members - five permanent (with veto rights), ten elected by the General Assembly for two year terms. Decisions binding on all UN members.
(IV) Representatives of all 193 Member States, each with one vote. Major decisions require a two thirds majority; otherwise a simple majority. Decisions not binding on UN members.

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For International Organisations (International Organisations in a Changing World):
Detailed Solution:
NCERT Class 12 Contemporary World Politics (Chapter 6: International Organisations, chart on 'Principal Organs of the United Nations', p. 85): (A) Security Council: 15 members - 5 permanent with veto, 10 non-permanent elected for 2 years; decisions are binding on all members (Match III). (B) General Assembly: 193 members, 1 vote each; non-binding resolutions (Match IV). (C) Secretariat: International civil service headed by the Secretary-General servicing UN organs (Match I). (D) Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC): 54 members elected by the General Assembly for overlapping 3-year terms (Match II). Matching: (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).
Hence, option (D) is the correct match.

Therefore, option (C) is the correct answer.
